notes.title: Engine Update: Better lighting AND better performance?
notes.notes:
The Godot Engine 4.4 has been released and comes with some long awaited, exciting features! 
Also in this release: Bugfixes, Optimizations and preparation for Internationalization and Sword Beach.

Performance

No more stuttering during runtime! Shaders are now pre-compiled during loading of a scene, which (mostly) prevents stuttering while exploring the museum.
The typewriter effect at the Audio Guide got an overhaul and is now more lightweight
Optimized LOD's
Optimized obstacle meshes at the Omaha Beach scene
Reworked Juno Beach, which resulted in ~5x more fps in some areas


Graphics

Lightmaps support now directional data aka normal maps, which results in more detailed objects


Gameplay

Added a new scene for first time users, to choose their VR Experience Level and apply some presets accordingly
Fixed a bug in Operation Albany, where other paratroopers wouldn't get deleted, after the scene ends. Which caused paratroopers lying around in all other scenes (xD)


Next Stop: Sword Beach

New Lightmaps

notes.title: Update 0.6 - Juno Beach
notes.notes:
This updated contains the following features:

- Juno Beach scene completed (for now)
- Implemented grabbing of objects
- Upgrade from Godot Engine 4.2 to 4.3, which should increase performance
- 3D scanned objects from Normandy
- 360-degree imagery from various places in Normandy
- New Loading Screen
- Several bugfixes and smaller additions

notes.title: Update 0.4
notes.notes:
The main features of this update are:

 Menus: Main Menu / Hub, Options and Credits
 Entrance: New walls, improved installations, decorations, ambient sound
 Entrance: New installation "StuG III and Panther D"
 Omaha: New walls, decorations, ambient sound, finished installations
 Improved Audioguide

The Main Menu also acts as a Hub, in which the player can quick-travel to all scenes.

notes.title: Update 0.3
notes.notes:
I'm excited to announce the latest milestone for the D-Day VR museum. Version 0.3 is now finished after four months of development, featuring a complete rebuild of Mulberry Harbour B in Normandy. This fully explorable harbor offers educational images, videos, text, and a virtual tour in a DUKW!
